teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). Official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Based on the published 2026/27 course offering, the language split is roughly: English ~57 CP, Italian ~39 CP, German ~36 CP of the mapped courses, i.e. English-leaning but with substantial Italian and German content. Critically, the ENTIRE first semester of year 1 is taught in English (Introduction to Programming 9 CP EN, Linear Algebra 6 CP EN, Discrete Mathematics 6 CP EN, Computer Systems Architecture 6 CP EN, English for Computer Scientists 3 CP EN = 30 CP, all EN). Italian and German enter from the second semester of year 1 (Analysis IT, Operating Systems M2 Programming in C IT, Web and Internet Engineering with Project DE). Later core courses in German include Software Engineering and Project (12 CP), Probability Theory and Statistics (6 CP) and Databases (12 CP); in Italian: Smart Software Systems (12 CP), Machine Learning (6 CP), Interactive Interface Design and Development (6 CP), Artificial Intelligence M1 (6 CP). Year 3 also has a compulsory 3 CP 'Italian for Computer Scientists / German for Computer Scientists' course. [uncertain] — exact credit weighting per language is derived from the 2026/27 course-offering page, which lists only the courses offered that year and not the full three-year plan.
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (Bruno-Buozzi-Straße 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Faculty of Engineering.
degree_class: L-31 (Scienze e tecnologie informatiche / Computer Science). 180 ECTS, 3 years.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered. The official programme page for 2026/27 states 'Courses will definetely be starting'. Both the Early Bird and the Late ranking lists for a.y. 2026/27 have already been published (20/05/2026 and 22/07/2026 respectively), confirming the intake actually ran.
is_new_programme: No — long-established programme. It was awarded the 'Bollino GRIN' quality label by the Italian GRuppo di INformatica in 2021. (Note: the separate, newly created sister programme at the same faculty is the Bachelor in Informatics and Management of Digital Business, first intake 2026/27 — not this one.)
majors_tracks_study_plans: No formal majors or separate study plans; a single study plan for all students. Specialisation happens through two elective 'Applied Computer Science Areas' in years 2-3 (Applied Computer Science 1 = 12 CP in year 2, Applied Computer Science 2 = 12 CP in year 3), chosen from: (1) Software and Systems Engineering — Smart Software Systems (12 CP: M1 Smart Software Design, M2 Smart Software Development) and Mobile and Physical Systems (12 CP: M1 Mobile Computing, M2 Prototyping Physical Interactive Experiences); (2) Intelligent Systems — Artificial Intelligence (12 CP: M1 Foundation of Artificial Intelligence, M2 Introduction to Computer Vision) and Intelligent Agents (12 CP: M1 Knowledge Representation, M2 Intelligent Agents Project). Plus 12 CP Free Choice in year 3. Part-time enrolment is available as an option. No dual-study four-year variant for this programme.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. This is the decisive filter: admission requires 'adequate knowledge of at least two of the teaching languages used in the study programme' at B2 level (1st language B2 AND 2nd language B2). A candidate who only knows English can certify at most one language and is therefore EXCLUDED FROM THE ADMISSION PROCEDURE, not merely ranked lower. Empirical proof from the published 2026/27 ranking lists: in the Early Bird session, ALL 26 non-EU applicants living abroad were excluded for failing the language requirements — zero non-EU admissions — and 19 EU/equivalent applicants were likewise excluded on language grounds. In the Late session a further 12 applicants were excluded for the same reason. Mitigating nuance: the second language does NOT have to be Italian or German at C1; the programme is genuinely accessible to someone with, for example, English B2 + German B2, or English B2 + Italian B2. A Turkish applicant with only English (even C1/C2) cannot be admitted. Note also the graduation requirement of C1/C1/B2 across all three languages.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit-based ranking list. There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no SAT, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is purely a documentary evaluation of secondary-school grades plus a small extracurricular bonus, carried out by an Admission Committee, followed by publication of a ranking list. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. A prior language-eligibility gate (B2 in two of the three teaching languages) excludes applicants before ranking.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) an Italian secondary school-leaving certificate; or (b) a foreign qualification recognised as equivalent. A foreign school-leaving certificate is considered equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (explicit example given: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after attending only one year is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research sets additional specific requirements for holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly; applicants in these categories should contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). In addition to the title, applicants must possess: (1) adequate general competence and disciplinary competence in the mathematical area — assessed from the average grade of the third-last and penultimate year of secondary school plus any other documents the commission requests; (2) adequate knowledge of at least two of the three teaching languages (B2 level — see language requirements). No specific ECTS/SSD credits apply (this is a bachelor programme). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed, but the two must not belong to the same class (e.g. not L-31/L-31) and must differ in at least 2/3 of the course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: NONE. There is no unibz aptitude/admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test for this programme. (This distinguishes it from the sister Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering, which does accept TOLC-I or CENT-S.) The only examinations connected to admission are LANGUAGE exams, and only for applicants who choose to prove proficiency that way: unibz Language Centre online language exams — Early Bird session 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late session 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Only B2-level exams can be registered for. Separately, AFTER admission there is a non-selective mathematics catch-up test for students assigned OFA, and a third-language placement test for admitted students who cannot certify their third language.
selection_scoring: Documentary scoring by the Admission Committee, maximum 11 points: up to 5 points for the evaluation of the average of all grades; up to 5 points for the evaluation of the average of grades in mathematics subjects; up to 1 point overall for proven extracurricular experiences in scientific/IT areas. Grades used are those of the third-last and penultimate year of secondary school, self-declared in the portal. Tie-break: in case of equal points, preference is given to the YOUNGER applicant. There is no published minimum passing threshold — the only hard eliminatory threshold is the language gate (B2 in two teaching languages); everything below that is ranked. A score of 3 points or less on the mathematics average does not exclude the candidate but triggers OFA. Special provision: if an applicant attended a school whose system differs substantially from the Italian system and lacks reports with final grades for the third-last and/or penultimate year, the Admission Committee reserves the right to evaluate final reports referring to other years. Competition level in 2026/27 was LOW for EU applicants: Early Bird admitted 31 people against 40 places, Late admitted 16 against the remaining places — i.e. essentially every language-eligible applicant was admitted.
bonus_points: Only one bonus mechanism: up to 1 point overall for proven extracurricular experiences in the scientific/IT field. A maximum of 2 certified experiences may be declared, using a self-declaration form provided in the application portal; for each experience a contact person must be indicated for verification. Examples given by unibz: participation in robotics competitions, mathematics Olympiads, computer competitions, online courses with certificate. There is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus and no startup-project bonus for this programme.
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no motivation letter, no video, no project proposal and no reference letters are required for this programme. The only structured upload beyond identity/school documents is the unibz-provided self-declaration form for a maximum of 2 certified extracurricular experiences in the science/IT field (contact person required for each). No file-size or page limits are published for this programme, because no portfolio-type materials exist. Grades for the third-last and penultimate school year are entered by self-declaration directly in the portal; if those years were completed abroad, copies of the relevant school report cards must be uploaded, with an official translation into Italian, German or English if needed.
interview: No interview. The admission procedure is entirely documentary; no interview dates are published for this programme.
conditional_admission: Applicants still attending their final year of secondary school apply and are ranked on the basis of their third-last and penultimate year grades, so admission before graduation is the normal case rather than a special regime. The secondary-school diploma is uploaded at enrolment, not at application ('if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'). Applicants with a foreign qualification are admitted 'con riserva' (with reserve): unibz verifies the foreign qualification at enrolment and the reserve is lifted if the title is deemed valid; if it does not permit enrolment the applicant is excluded — and exclusion by Rector's decree is possible even AFTER enrolment if the admission qualification turns out to be invalid. Refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are not refundable except if the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam (maturità) or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. [uncertain] — the ≥120/140 ECTS conditional-admission rule referenced in the field schema is a MASTER-level rule and does not apply here; no equivalent numeric threshold and no 11/12/2026 late-enrolment window is published in this programme's admission document.
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) applies to this programme in the MATHEMATICS area. Trigger: applicants who obtain 3 points or less out of 5 for the evaluation of the average of mathematics grades are assigned OFA as part of the admission procedure — the OFA assignment is marked with an asterisk directly in the published ranking list (4 of 31 admitted in Early Bird 2026 and 2 of 16 in the Late session carried an asterisk). Remedy: attend the Faculty's mathematics catch-up course BEFORE the start of the 'Linear Algebra' course and pass the relevant test. If the test is failed, the student follows an individual study programme agreed with a tutor and must still complete the OFA within the first year by passing the test or, alternatively, the 'Linear Algebra' exam. Consequence of non-completion: the student may enrol in the second year but CANNOT take any second- or third-year exams. Note this is distinct from the mathematics-test OFA used in the economics programmes; here it is grade-based, not test-based.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language rule is eliminatory: failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank. Entry: B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language; no level required in the 3rd language. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2. Language positions are defined by the applicant's own proficiency, not by the language: the 1st language is the one in which the applicant is strongest, the 3rd the weakest (possibly absolute beginner). Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Because the first semester of this programme is taught only in English, an applicant whose THIRD language is English must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to be able to take all first-semester curricular exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2; A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY during the September pre-semester intensive session (01-18/09/2026, Mon-Fri, 6 h/day), so absolute beginners must start there. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test and are assigned a learning path. During the semesters there are extensive courses (4 h/week) and between semesters intensive courses (6 h/day); all Language Centre courses are free of charge.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required (B1 needed only to sit curricular exams in that language; B1 in English by mid-January if English is the third language, because semester 1 is English-only). This is the 'B2/B2/none' pattern shared with the other trilingual engineering bachelors, and is one step lower than the C1/B2/none pattern used by programmes such as Public Policy and Accounting and Finance. Position is determined by the candidate's own strength ranking, not by which language it is; only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is the standard unibz trilingual exit profile and is a real graduation gate, not an aspiration — a student admitted with B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third during the three years. Language Centre courses are free and structured to support this (B1 in the third language by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2).
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language. Programme-specific escalation: because the first semester of the Bachelor in Computer Science is taught ONLY in English, a student whose third language is English must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January in order to sit all curricular exams scheduled for the first semester.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways: (1) the main teaching language of the final year of high school, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter/document from the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload their certificates and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, registered online through the application portal ('enrol for language exams') after creating an application — Early Bird: exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); only B2-level exams can be registered for. Additional route for bi-/multilingual and foreign schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language, subject to Language Centre approval. Administrative detail: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'). Rules: (1) the certificate must include assessment in ALL FOUR skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must indicate adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall result/level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL determines the recognised level, provided that part was passed; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION for failed exam parts and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides them; (5) certificates obtained by taking an online 'home edition' exam are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged in the list (a small number of LanguageCert ESOL and MET items carry the 'also accepted as home edition' asterisk); (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and exams from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised. Validity: international language certificates must not be older than FIVE YEARS at the date of submission (the entire calendar year counts from 1 January of the fifth preceding year). Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). Early Bird Application: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. Late Application (EU only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. Additional Application Session (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only if places remain): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the Early Bird Application, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, and they pay a non-refundable €50 application fee. They are ranked on a separate ranking list against a separate 4-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) for the study visa.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants (this is the critical third category for Turkish applicants): (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of Legislative Decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a tourist visa is NOT sufficient. If the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. Critical warning: if the permit is not uploaded in the application portal, the applicant is AUTOMATICALLY treated as a non-EU citizen living abroad and is placed on the separate non-EU ranking list, subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in the country of origin — losing access to the Late and Additional sessions and the 50-place EU quota.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application 40 places, Late Application 10 places (50 EU in total — the brochure and programme page summarise this as 'Places available: 50 EU + 4 non-EU'). Non-EU citizens living abroad: Early Bird Application 4 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule: for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only, any places remaining unfilled after the Early Bird session are offered in the Late Application. Actual 2026/27 uptake: 31 EU/equivalent admitted in Early Bird (against 40 places), 16 EU/equivalent admitted in the Late session, and ZERO non-EU applicants admitted in either session — all 26 non-EU Early Bird applicants were excluded for not meeting the language requirements.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (the signed list is actually dated Bolzano, 20/05/2026); payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees (€600, this is what secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 06/08/2026 noon. Late Application: ranking lists published by 30/07/2026 (signed list dated 22/07/2026); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 noon. Additional Application Session: ranking lists by 18/09/2026; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 25/09/2026 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice. Paying the fee does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (exceptions: failing the maturità, or, for non-EU applicants abroad, not obtaining the documents from the Italian authorities). Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Bolzano within 60 days of notification or publication.
programme_specific_dates: Preparatory and start-of-year dates for 2026/27: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day); pre-courses 21/09-09/10/2026; Freshers Days 28-29/09/2026. Academic calendar: 1st semester classes 28/09-23/12/2026, holidays 24/12/2026-06/01/2027, classes resume 07-23/01/2027, exams 25/01-20/02/2027; 2nd semester classes 01/03-25/03/2027, holidays 26-29/03/2027, classes 30/03-12/06/2027, exams 14/06-10/07/2027; autumn exam session 23/08-25/09/2027. Programme-specific admission-linked dates are limited to the Language Centre exam sessions (16/03/2026; 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026; 22-26/06/2026) and the mid-January English B1 deadline for students whose third language is English. There are no programme-specific entrance-exam, interview or portfolio-submission dates because none of those instruments are used. Third-language placement test: date communicated by e-mail to admitted students. Signed ranking-list dates: 20/05/2026 (Early Bird) and 22/07/2026 (Late).
required_documents: At application (online, via https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document causes exclusion from the admission procedure; the completed online form; self-declared subjects and grades for the third-last and penultimate year of secondary school; copies of the relevant school report cards if those years were completed abroad, with an official translation into Italian, German or English if needed; the unibz self-declaration form for up to 2 certified extracurricular experiences in the science/IT field, with a contact person named for each (optional, worth up to 1 point); language certificates uploaded under the corresponding menu item (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended for the 3rd) or registration for Language Centre exams; the diploma of the qualification if already obtained abroad; for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay (plus renewal request if expired). NOTE: there is NO 'study career' Excel template for this programme — that structured upload is a master-level requirement. At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload: the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English); and, depending on the education system, the ARDI Statement of Correspondence and/or CIMEA statements (see credential_recognition). Once the application is submitted it CANNOT be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly NON-REFUNDABLE. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay) pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, in two instalments: 1st instalment €600 (which includes the €16 revenue stamp / marca da bollo) — this is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, to be paid by March of the following year. Late payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (certificate from the health authorities to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Fees pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-computer-science_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: Main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario / Office for Higher Education Support), applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. The province offers three instruments: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — so a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships at bachelor level (disability, Italian government scholarship holders). No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Bachelor in Computer Science. [uncertain] — the frequently cited grant range of roughly €1,680-€6,960 per year and any merit thresholds (e.g. a 27/30 average after the first year) could not be confirmed on the pages verified for this programme; amounts are set annually by the provincial call, which should be checked directly. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. Reference page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. unibz performs its own checks on the foreign qualification and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; applicants with a foreign title are admitted with reserve until the check clears, and an applicant found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only (€50 non-refundable fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (4 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by the published deadline → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal of the Ministry of University and Research. The Universitaly pre-enrolment is MANDATORY: without it, both the application and the enrolment made at the university are void, and only ONE programme may be selected on Universitaly. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. Explicit caveats from unibz: admission to unibz does not guarantee a visa or even an appointment, since visas are the exclusive competence of embassies and consulates, and holding a study visa confers no automatic right to complete enrolment. Financial means required for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing), excluding tuition fees; total proof of at least €36,000 for a bachelor programme (€24,000 for a master). Health insurance is required. After arrival: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service / Student Support immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. Universitaly: https://www.universitaly.it/
official_call_url: No separate call for applications / manifesto degli studi document is published for this programme. The role of the official call is played by the programme's admission-information document (https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-computer-science_admission-information_en_GB.pdf) together with the signed ranking-list decrees, which carry the selection criteria, the Admission Committee signatures (Chair Prof. Alessandro Artale; members Prof. Sergio Tessaris, Prof. Andrea Janes) and the 60-day appeal notice to the Administrative Court of Bolzano. General applicant portal: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz ; application portal: https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ . uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 03.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change.' Verified as of 2026-08-29 — note that the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 have already CLOSED and their ranking lists are published; only the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026, EU only, if places remain) may still be open at the time of verification. (1) Apparent places conflict: the programme page and brochure say '50 EU + 4 non-EU' while the admission-information PDF splits EU places into 40 Early Bird + 10 Late. These reconcile (40+10=50); the PDF split is authoritative for per-session planning. An earlier automated reading of the HTML page reported '50 Early Bird + 10 Late' — that is wrong. (2) Teaching-language weighting is reconstructed from the 2026/27 course-offering listing, which shows only the courses actually offered that year (year-3 courses such as Formal Languages and Compilers, Information Security, Computational Mathematics for Data Science and the Italian/German for Computer Scientists course carry no published language tag in that view), so the per-language credit totals are indicative rather than official. The finding that year-1 semester 1 is 100% English is solid: all five semester-1 first-year courses are tagged EN and the admission PDF's mid-January English-B1 clause is written for exactly this situation. (3) Scholarship amounts are not confirmed for 2026/27 — the €1,680-€6,960 range and any merit-average threshold come from secondary summaries, not from a page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually. (4) No formal 'conditional admission' regime with an ECTS threshold exists at bachelor level; the master-level ≥120/140 ECTS rule and the 11/12/2026 late-enrolment window in the field schema do not apply here. (5) No separate call/manifesto document was found in English; a Rector's decree may exist only in the Italian albo. (6) No 'study career' Excel template applies to this bachelor programme. (7) The self-declaration form for extracurricular experiences is distributed inside the application portal and has no public standalone URL, so its exact format limits could not be recorded. (8) The €7,002.84 figure sometimes quoted for residence-permit renewal appeared only in a search summary and was not confirmed on a unibz page, so it is excluded from the visa field. (9) Turkish-applicant relevance: Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so case (b) recognition applies — this classification is inferred from the convention's membership, not stated by unibz for this programme.
